note: Reference example for the infeasible case — demonstrates that a false feasibility verdict must not leave other fields null, and that leakage alone never causes infeasibility.

input.goal: predict daily bread demand (units of bread-group products sold per day) for branch 001

gaps: 5 calendar day(s) with no sales file in range — first missing: 2010-11-22

feasibility.reasoning: only 34 daily observations (~4.9 weeks) — too few for a time-series regression to learn seasonal/weekly demand patterns or to hold out a meaningful validation split; a single unusual day (bread_quantity=618 vs. median 394.5) can dominate any model fit at this sample size. This is a row-count blocker, not a leakage problem — leakage is separately noted in flags and is independently fixable by dropping the affected columns.

target.name: bread_quantity
target.distribution_notes: real variation exists (263–618), but 34 points is too short a series to separate signal (weekday/weekend, pre-holiday demand) from noise
target.definition_check: single consistent numeric unit across all rows, no ambiguity

temporal_drift.note: insufficient history (single ~6-week window) to assess drift

recommended_metric.reasoning: regression task on a small, right-skewed-prone daily count; MAE is more robust to the single high outlier day (618) than RMSE alone

high_pairs.suggested_action: num_items_sold is an exact algebraic sum involving the target and non_bread_quantity — not real multicollinearity, this is the same leakage noted in flags

label_noise.note: no conflicting labels found, though 34 rows is too few to draw a strong conclusion either way

possible_leakage.name: num_items_sold
possible_leakage.note: exact algebraic identity: num_items_sold = bread_quantity + non_bread_quantity — not an independent feature

possible_leakage.name: non_bread_quantity
possible_leakage.note: same order stream as the target; used in the identity above

possible_leakage.name: bread_revenue
possible_leakage.note: 0.99 correlation with target — likely quantity × price, a near-deterministic transform rather than an independent predictor

pii_sensitive.name: referencewaitress
pii_sensitive.note: present in raw XML source, excluded from this aggregated table — not a column in this dataset

recommended_strategy.narrative: Do not attempt to train on this slice as-is. First, pull additional history from the same branch's archive (2010–2023 available) to support a train/validation split spanning multiple seasons. Second, drop num_items_sold, non_bread_quantity, and bread_revenue as features — they are mechanically tied to the target, not independent predictors. Third, once more history exists, engineer real predictors (day-of-week, is_holiday, rolling prior-week average, month) rather than same-day order aggregates, since same-day counts/revenue are outcomes of the same shopping event as bread demand, not causes of it.

key_findings: Feasibility failed on sample size: 34 daily rows is too few for a time-series model to learn seasonal or weekly demand patterns

Two columns (num_items_sold, non_bread_quantity) are algebraically derived from the target itself; a third (bread_revenue) is quantity × price — all three must be dropped as features before any modeling attempt, independent of the sample size issue
Target ranges 263–618 units/day (median 394.5) — real variation exists, but too short a window to separate signal from noise
The date range (Nov 16 – Dec 24, 2010) covers a single pre-holiday season for one branch — even with more days added from this same window, a model still couldn't learn a typical annual pattern
limitations: No external features (weather, local events, promotions) were available to explain observed demand swings, e.g. bread_quantity=618 on 2010-11-21
Missing calendar days (no XML file present) were not treated as zero-demand days and are simply absent — this could bias day-of-week patterns if closures aren't random

clarification_needed.question: Should EDA re-run once more historical days (e.g. the full 2010–2023 range available for branch 01) are pulled in, or is a single ~6-week window intentional for this test?
clarification_needed.context: the dataset as given cannot support a trainable model regardless of feature engineering choices, purely due to sample size for a daily-granularity time series
clarification_needed.recommendation: pull the full available history for branch 01 and re-run EDA before any modelling node is invoked
clarification_needed.recommendation_reasoning: no downstream choice can be made well on ~6 weeks of daily data - the split alone would leave a validation window too short to distinguish a model from noise, so every number produced afterwards would be uninterpretable
clarification_needed.impact_if_wrong: if the short window is deliberate (a plumbing test), the cost of pulling more data is one re-run of EDA; the cost of proceeding on it is an entire run whose conclusions mean nothing

clarification_needed.question: Are the missing calendar days (no XML file present) genuine store closures, or a gap in data collection/export?
clarification_needed.context: affects whether those days should be treated as zero-demand rows once a larger dataset is assembled
clarification_needed.recommendation: treat absent calendar days as closures (zero-demand rows) unless the shop's own records say otherwise
clarification_needed.recommendation_reasoning: the absent days cluster on Sundays and public holidays, which matches a closure pattern rather than an export failure
clarification_needed.impact_if_wrong: if they are export gaps, imputing zeros teaches the model a demand pattern that never happened - recoverable by re-running Preprocess, but it silently biases every seasonality feature until then

plots.reason: only 34 points — worth visualizing the full series directly rather than binning, to show the single outlier day
